issues.body:
SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS (line 1634) is the single source of truth for what the enrolled suite executes: today `jq|command|jq|...` and `PyYAML|pymodule|yaml|...`. _selftest_env_blocked keys the ENV-BLOCKED refusal off that table alone.

_assert_worker_image_gate_deps instead hard-codes one frozen string, 'RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends jq python3-yaml && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*', and its own comment encodes today's table size as a constant ("must provision BOTH executables").

So the two are coupled by nothing but coincidence. Add a third row to SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS -- exactly the change this gate's history says keeps happening (#824, #1371, #1346) -- and: the model image does not provision it, the author-side gate goes back to ENV-BLOCKED, the agent is back to root-causing artifact rows by hand, and this assertion stays green the whole time. The check reports 'provisioned' while the invariant it names is false.

This is the same defect shape as the one _assert_actionlint_pin_single_sourced was written to forbid, one lane over: the comment at :2360 insists actionlint come 'from the same single-source scripts/actionlint.pin pr-gate.yml reads, so the two lanes cannot lint with different actionlints', and :1367-1371 rejects a workflow that re-inlines its own version+checksum. This PR re-inlines the dependency set.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the expectation from the table rather than restating it. E.g. map each SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS row to its apt package via one small lookup (jq->jq, PyYAML->python3-yaml) and assert that every row's package appears in the image's install instruction, failing closed on a row with no mapping -- an unmapped requirement must refuse, never read as satisfied (same posture as _selftest_dep_present's `*) return 1`). Then add a self-test fixture that injects a synthetic third requirement row and proves the assertion goes RED against the current Dockerfile; that fixture is what makes the coupling real rather than asserted in a comment.
issues.title: Dependency set is re-inlined as a frozen literal instead of derived from SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS

issues.body:
The three new chks (:5301-5317) drive _assert_worker_image_gate_deps directly. Nothing asserts that registry_selftest_gate actually CALLS it, or that it DIEs rather than warning.

I confirmed the gap is real: grep for the symbol finds it only at the definition (:1799), the call site (:2393), and the three direct chks. The exact-block dispatch pin at :8770 does not cover it either -- _registry_gate_selftest_dispatch (:1329-1332) emits only blocks whose text contains 'run_enrolled_selftest' or 'self-test', and the new dockerfile-loop block contains neither (the die string says '...for the registry gate'). So removing lines 2392-2395 is a silent no-op across the entire suite.

That is precisely the failure mode this file documents at :8746-8751 -- 'a guard whose call sites are unpinned can be bypassed without a single row going red' -- and the reason #824 and #524 both carry wiring pins. The nearest analogue is exact: _assert_workflow_actions_pinned sits in the sibling touched-workflow loop of this same gate and got both a 'calls the pin assertion' and a 'REFUSES, does not warn and continue' pin (:5421-5424).

Honest caveat: the older sibling _assert_dockerfile_pinned (#145) is also unwired, so this PR matches local precedent in that one loop. I still rate it major because #524/#824 and the :8746 comment are the later, explicit standard, and this PR is adding a new guard rather than inheriting an old one.
issues.fix_hint:
Mirror the #524 pattern next to the new chks:

  gate_body=$(declare -f registry_selftest_gate)
  chk "#1575 wiring: the dockerfile lint calls the model-image dependency assertion" \
    "$(printf '%s\n' "$gate_body" | grep -c '_assert_worker_image_gate_deps')" "1"
  chk "#1575 wiring: an under-provisioned model image REFUSES the gate, it does not warn and continue" \
    "$(printf '%s\n' "$gate_body" | grep -c 'die "worker model image does not provision')" "1"

Note `gate_body` is already declared local earlier in the suite (:4208, :5420), so reuse it rather than redeclaring.
issues.title: New call site in registry_selftest_gate is unpinned: deleting it leaves the whole suite green

issues.body:
_assert_worker_image_gate_deps collects EVERY normalised RUN instruction in the file and passes if the expected literal appears anywhere in that set. It never asks which build stage the instruction belongs to, nor whether a later instruction undoes it.

Two diffs therefore pass while the runtime image lacks jq and PyYAML:

  FROM debian:bookworm@sha256:... AS unused
  RUN apt-get update && apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends jq python3-yaml && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  FROM rust:1.88.0-bookworm@sha256:...
  COPY --from=node /usr/local/bin/node /usr/local/bin/node

and the same install in the final stage followed by `RUN apt-get purge --yes jq`. Both are accepted; the model container still cannot run the suite.

The function comment claims the complete-instruction match makes 'deleting either package, moving the install behind a condition, or retaining apt metadata all fail closed', which is accurate as far as it goes -- I verified all three. Stage relocation and later removal are simply outside what the match can see, and the comment reads as a stronger totality claim than the code supports. Rated minor rather than major because this guard is developer ergonomics (the host-side pr-gate preflight remains the load-bearing refusal) and because the bypass requires deliberate restructuring.
issues.fix_hint: Track the FROM boundaries in the same awk pass and only emit RUN instructions belonging to the last stage, then assert the expected instruction is present there and that no later instruction in that stage removes the packages (reject `apt-get remove|purge` and `rm ` targeting the installed binaries). Add two fixtures: the install parked in a discarded first stage, and the install followed by a purge -- both must return 'absent'. Also tighten the function comment to state what the match does and does not cover.
issues.title: Assertion is not stage-scoped and ignores later removal, so it can report 'provisioned' for an image that provisions nothing

issues.body:
This file exists to keep the model-isolation sandbox reproducible: both FROMs are digest-pinned, _assert_dockerfile_pinned enforces that on every touched container definition (#145: 'so a benign-labelled PR cannot silently weaken the model-isolation sandbox'), and the self-test rejects variable-expanded, short, non-hex, and empty digests.

`apt-get update && apt-get install jq python3-yaml` resolves to whatever the Debian bookworm archive serves at build time. Two runners building the same commit can get different sandbox contents, and the digest pin above no longer describes the image the model actually runs in. The repo's own standard for provisioning a tool is stricter: _ensure_actionlint fetches a 'pinned, sha256-verified release' from a single-source pin file precisely so the two lanes cannot diverge.

Integrity is not broken here -- apt GPG-verifies against the keyring baked into the digest-pinned base -- so this is a reproducibility regression, not a supply-chain hole, which is why it is minor and not a blocker. Worth stating explicitly rather than leaving implied.

Separately, and non-blocking: this adds a Python interpreter to the untrusted model's sandbox. Given the container already ships node plus the full rust/cargo/gcc toolchain, that is not a meaningful escalation.
issues.fix_hint: Either pin the versions (`apt-get install --yes --no-install-recommends jq=1.6-2.1 python3-yaml=6.0-3+b2`) so the image is reproducible, or leave it unpinned deliberately and say so in the comment -- 'versions intentionally float; integrity chains through the digest-pinned base image's apt keyring, reproducibility is traded for not having to bump two pins per Debian point release'. Note that version-pinning interacts with issue (1): whatever form is chosen, keep the expected string derived from one source rather than restated in the assertion.
issues.title: Unpinned apt packages introduced into the one file whose purpose is pin enforcement

issues.body:
Because the whole normalised instruction must match byte-for-byte, all of these fail the gate despite provisioning exactly the right packages: `-y` instead of `--yes`; `python3-yaml jq` instead of `jq python3-yaml`; splitting the install across two RUN lines; adding a third package; dropping the (redundant-under-BuildKit) apt-lists cleanup.

The strictness is deliberate and it is what makes the deps-inert fixture work, so this is a nit, not a defect. But it means a future author's first encounter with this check is likely to be a confusing failure on a change that is correct, and the die message ('does not provision jq + PyYAML for the registry gate') will not tell them that the problem is formatting rather than a missing package.
issues.fix_hint: Make the die message name the expected instruction verbatim, e.g. `die "worker model image RUN instruction does not match the expected provisioning line exactly (formatting counts): $name -- expected: <literal>"`. If issue (1) is fixed by deriving from SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS, prefer asserting per-package presence within a single unconditional install instruction over whole-string equality; that keeps the deps-inert rejection (the `false &&` prefix is still not part of an unconditional install) while tolerating reordering and `-y`.
issues.title: Exact-literal match rejects benign, semantically identical reformatting

verdict.summary:
The premise is sound and the fixtures are genuinely non-vacuous. The model container really is where the enrolled suite is ENV-BLOCKED today (SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS at worker-live.sh:1634 lists exactly jq + PyYAML; the comment at :1620 records that ~a third of the suite is unrunnable in the container), python3-yaml pulls python3 so the pymodule probe is satisfied, and the awk normaliser correctly folds the real multi-line RUN into the expected literal. I verified both reject fixtures flip red for the right reason: deps-missing loses 'python3-yaml' from the exact string, deps-inert gains a leading 'false && '. This is not a vacuous test, and it does not weaken any existing trust check. The new dockerfile-loop block also does not disturb the exact-block dispatch pin at :8770, because _registry_gate_selftest_dispatch only emits blocks containing 'run_enrolled_selftest' or 'self-test' and the new die string contains neither.

Two majors block approval, both about the assertion drifting silently rather than being wrong today.

(1) The dependency set is re-inlined as a frozen literal instead of being derived from SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS, which is the single source the preflight actually keys on. Add a third requirement row and the model image is under-provisioned again while this assertion stays green -- the exact re-inlining that _assert_actionlint_pin_single_sourced exists to forbid one lane over.

(2) The new call site has no wiring pin. The three new chks exercise the pure function only; deleting the two-line call at :2392-2395 leaves the entire suite green. The closest analogue in the same gate, _assert_workflow_actions_pinned, did get wiring pins (#524 wiring, :5421-5424), as did the #824 preflight, and the comment at :8746 states the rule outright.

Two minors on soundness and on introducing unpinned package content into the file whose whole purpose is pinning. Nothing token-shaped, no permissions or workflow-expansion surface touched.
